{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|ja|八幡宮}} == External Links == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also
