{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}}== See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}}== See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also! == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|ja|八幡宮}} == External Links == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|ja|八幡宮}} == External Links == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命)
{{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命)
{{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ja|館山市}} neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}}. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it held the rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|ja|八幡宮}} == External Links == * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:word=11010 Official website] (Japanese) {{draft categories| [[Category:C114]] [[Category: Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 5]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category: 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:1 revision imported]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:null edit to force updates]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:S11]] [[Category:return the see also]] }} [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[en:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] [[sn:suruya Hachiman Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine}}

{{神社 |名称 = 鶴谷八幡宮 |画像 = [[File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG|250px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[千葉県]][[館山市]][[八幡 (館山市)|八幡]]68 |位置 = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[応神天皇|品陀和気命]]
[[仲哀天皇|帯中津彦命]]
[[神功皇后|息長帯姫命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[安房国]][[総社]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = [[平安時代]]初期 |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = 9月[[敬老の日]]前の土日 |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=鶴谷八幡宮|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210|coord={{coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E}}}} }} [[ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|thumb|220px|鳥居]] '''鶴谷八幡宮'''（つるがやはちまんぐう）は、[[千葉県]][[館山市]][[八幡 (館山市)|八幡]]にある[[神社]]。[[安房国]][[総社]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の3柱。 * 品陀和気命（[[応神天皇]]） * 帯中津彦命（[[仲哀天皇]]） * 息長帯姫命（[[神功皇后]]） == 歴史 == [[ファイル:Moto-hachiman-jinja (Minamiboso).JPG|thumb|220px|元八幡神社（[[南房総市]]府中）。元宮といわれ、一帯に安房国府も推定される。]] [[平安時代]]初期、[[国府]]近くの現在の[[南房総市]]府中に'''安房国総社'''として創建された。[[鎌倉時代]]に入ると総社信仰が衰微し、代わって[[源氏]]の影響で[[八幡神]]信仰が高まったため、総社から改変され八幡宮となり、当初の位置から遷座するに至ったという。[[康応]]2年（[[1390年]]）には、'''安西八幡宮'''の名で資料に見える。 中世には[[里見氏]]、[[江戸時代]]には[[江戸幕府|徳川幕府]]の崇敬を受け、社殿奉納や社領寄進を受けている。[[明治]]6年（[[1873年]]）には郷社、[[昭和]]15年（[[1940年]]）には県社に列せられた。創建1000年を迎えた昭和51年（[[1976年]]）の本殿改修に当たって、'''鶴谷八幡宮'''と改称している。 == 境内 == [[ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, shaden.JPG|thumb|220px|社殿。中央に拝殿、右奥に本殿。]] [[国道127号]]に面して大鳥居が聳え、参道沿いには[[日露戦争]]ゆかりの記念碑が並ぶ。 * 本殿 - [[享保]]5年（[[1721年]]）造営。館山市指定文化財{{Cite book|和書|author=|title=館山市の文化財|publisher=館山市教育委員会・館山市文化財保護協会|year=2016-3-31|page=34|isbn=}}。 * 幣殿 - 昭和7年（[[1932年]]）造営。前社殿は[[関東大震災]]で倒壊。　 * 拝殿 - 幣殿に同じ。 * 社務所 ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|本殿（館山市指定文化財） ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, chokoku.JPG|拝殿天井の彫刻「百態の龍」（館山市指定文化財） ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|安房神社遥拝所 ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, entrance.JPG|境内鳥居 == 摂末社 == [[ファイル:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, Wakamiya-hachiman-sha.JPG|thumb|220px|若宮八幡神社]] * 若宮八幡神社 - 祭神：大雀命（[[仁徳天皇]]） * 高良神社 - 祭神：[[武内宿禰|武内宿禰命]] * 鹿島神社 - 祭神：[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌命]] * 西宮神社 - 祭神：[[事代主|事代主命]] == 祭事 == === 年間祭事 === * 歳旦祭（1月1日） * 筒粥神事（1月15日） * 節分祭（2月） * 祈念祭（2月17日） * 虫送り神事、大祓（6月30日） * 風神祭（8月30日） * 例大祭（9月14日、15日） * 新嘗祭（11月23日） * 大祓（12月31日） === 例大祭 === 国司祭（[[国府祭]]）の伝統を引き継ぎ1000年以上行われている祭で、[[千葉県指定文化財一覧#無形民俗文化財|千葉県無形民俗文化財]]に指定されている。通称「'''やわたんまち'''（八幡祭）」。[[南房総]]を代表する祭である。初日には安房国南部10社の[[神輿]]が入り、翌日に市内5町から[[山車]]・お船が出る。夕刻には10社の神輿の還御、及び八幡宮神輿の御浜出が催行される。 2019年（令和元年）は9月14日から15日での開催が予定されていたが、同年9月9日に[[房総半島]]に接近した[[令和元年房総半島台風]]（台風15号）の影響で館山市や南房総市内に甚大な被害が発生したことを受けて、神輿や山車・お船の出祭は取りやめとなり、鶴谷八幡宮内での祭典のみに縮小。記録上初めての中止となった{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.bonichi.com/News/item.htm?iid=13060|title=「やわたんまち」中止に 祭典のみ開催へ 館山|accessdate=2019年9月12日|publisher=房日新聞（2019年9月11日作成）}}。 2020年（令和2年）についても、[[SARSコロナウイルス2|新型コロナウイルス]]感染拡大防止の観点から、前年と同様に宮内での祭典のみに縮小したため、2年連続での神輿や山車・お船の出祭中止を余儀なくされた{{Cite web|和書|url=https://tsurugaya-hachimangu.org/topics/|title=令和二年例大祭・安房国司祭（宮入取りやめ）のお知らせ|accessdate=2020-09-09|publisher=|website=鶴谷八幡宮|date=2020-06-27}}。 2021年（令和3年）も引き続きコロナウイルス感染拡大防止の為、3年連続で神輿や山車・お船の出祭は中止になった{{Cite web|和書|title=やわたんまちの宮入りは中止 館山|url=https://bonichi.com/2021/07/15/19668/?hilite=%27%E3%82%84%E3%82%8F%E3%81%9F%E3%82%93%E3%81%BE%E3%81%A1%27|website=房日新聞|accessdate=2021-10-17|date=2021-07-15}}。八幡宮の神輿は4年ぶりに担がれ一の鳥居にて、神幸祭を行った。 2022年（令和4年）は、コロナウイルス感染拡大防止のため安房南部10社の神輿の出祭は4年連続で中止となったが、山車は5年ぶりに引き回され、久しぶりに北条地区に祭り囃子が奏でられた{{Cite web|和書|title=4年ぶりに"やわたんまち" |url=https://bonichi.com/2022/09/18/230056/ |website=[[房日新聞]]電子版 |publisher=房州日日新聞社 |date=2022-09-18 |accessdate=2023-09-11}}。八幡宮の神輿は前年と同じく担ぎだされ、八幡海岸にて神幸祭を行った。また、八幡宮の境内にも露天商が出店し賑やかなお祭りとなった。 == 文化財 == === 千葉県指定文化財 === * 無形民俗文化財 ** 安房やわたんまち - 平成16年3月30日指定[https://www.pref.chiba.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/bunkazai/p321-062.html 安房やわたんまち]（千葉県ホームページ）。。 === 館山市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財[http://www.city.tateyama.chiba.jp/syougaigaku/page000790.html 館山市の指定文化財（指定年月日順）]（館山市ホームページ）。 ** 鶴谷八幡神社本殿（建造物） - 昭和42年2月21日指定。 ** 鶴谷八幡神社百態の龍（彫刻） - 昭和49年2月21日指定。 ** 刀 銘「守家」（工芸品） - 昭和58年10月25日指定。 ** 鶴谷八幡神社棟札 3枚（考古資料） - [[館山市立博物館]]に保管。昭和40年4月21日指定。 * 無形民俗文化財 ** 鶴谷八幡宮の筒粥神事 - 平成5年12月24日指定。 === 関連文化財 === * 元八幡神社 - 南房総市指定史跡。平成3年9月10日指定[https://www.city.minamiboso.chiba.jp/0000000913.html 南房総市指定文化財]（南房総市ホームページ）。。 * 元八幡神社御清水送りの儀式 - 南房総市指定無形民俗文化財。平成3年9月10日指定。 == 現地情報 == ; 所在地 :* [[千葉県]][[館山市]][[八幡 (館山市)|八幡]]68 ; 交通アクセス :* 鉄道：[[東日本旅客鉄道]]（JR東日本）[[内房線]] [[館山駅]]から、北へ約1キロメートル == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 関連項目 == * [[千葉県の神社一覧]] * [[八幡宮#関東地方|八幡宮]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Tsurugaya-Hachiman-gū}} * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=11010 鶴谷八幡宮] - 千葉県神社庁監修「神社のひろば」 * [http://history.hanaumikaidou.com/archives/3795 鶴谷八幡宮] - 館山市立博物館「たてやまフィールドミュージアム」 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:つるかやはちまんくう}} [[Category:千葉県の神社]] [[Category:館山市の歴史]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:安房国|社01]] [[Category:八幡信仰]] [[Category:八幡宮]] [[Category:千葉県の旧県社]] [[Category:館山市の建築物]] [[Category:都道府県指定無形民俗文化財]] [[カテゴリ:房総の魅力500選]]

Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保|qq=draft|qq=draft}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja|ja|総社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awa Province (Chiba)|qq=}}. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman|qq=}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūai|qq=}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awa Province (Chiba)|qq=}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamibōsō|qq=}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamoto clan|qq=}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satomi clan|qq=}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|qq=}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōhō era|qq=}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|qq=}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateyama Station|qq=}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uchibō Line|qq=}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|ja|八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman shrine|qq=}} == External Links == * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:word=11010 Official website] (Japanese) {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|鶴谷八幡宮|version=101066790|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:C114]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:null edit to force updates]] }} [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[en:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] [[sn:suruya Hachiman Shrine]]

Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|応神天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman|qq=}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chūai|qq=}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|ja|安房国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awa Province (Chiba)|qq=}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|ja|南房総市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamibōsō|qq=}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minamoto clan|qq=}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|ja|里見氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satomi clan|qq=}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|qq=}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō era|ja|享保|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōhō era|qq=}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|qq=}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station|ja|館山駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tateyama Station|qq=}} on the [[JR East]] {{ill|Uchibō Line|ja|内房線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uchibō Line|qq=}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|ja|八幡宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman shrine|qq=}} == External Links == * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:word=11010 Official website] (Japanese) {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|鶴谷八幡宮|version=101066790|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:null edit to force updates]] [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]]}} [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[en:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] [[sn:suruya Hachiman Shrine]]

Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命)
[[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命)
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama, Chiba]] neighborhood of Hachiman in [[Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|qq=}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takenouchi no Sukune|Takenouchi no Sukune]]. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]]. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi]]. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|qq=}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|qq=}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|qq=}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of [[:en:Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Tateyama Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[:en:Uchibō Line|Uchibō Line]]. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} * [[:en:Hachiman shrine|Hachiman shrine]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:word=11010 Official website] (Japanese) {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|鶴谷八幡宮|version=101066790|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:null edit to force updates]] [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]]}} [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[en:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] [[sn:suruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[Category:Hachiman faith]] [[Category:Hachiman shrines]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Chiba Prefecture]]

Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|qq=}} during the [[Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building.
