Haiden | location = [[Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[Tateyama]], [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|18.8|N|139|52|0|E|display=inline,title}} | deity = [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命)
[[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命)
[[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命) | founding = Early [[Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama, Chiba]] neighborhood of Hachiman in [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takenouchi no Sukune|Takenouchi no Sukune]]. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]]. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi]]. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鶴谷八幡宮}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|qq=}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of [[:en:Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Tateyama Station]] on the [[JR East]] [[:en:Uchibō Line|Uchibō Line]]. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|qq=}} * [[:en:Hachiman shrine|Hachiman shrine]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:word=11010 Official website] (Japanese) {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|鶴谷八幡宮|version=101066790|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]]}} [[sn:Tsuruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] [[sn:suruya Hachiman Shrine]] [[Category:Hachiman faith]] [[Category:Hachiman shrines]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:Awa Province (Chiba)]] [[Category:房総の魅力500選]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Buildings in Tateyama, Chiba]] [[Category:History of Tateyama, Chiba]] {{Commons category|Tsurugaya-Hachiman-gū}}

Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[:en:Respect for the Aged Day|Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|qid=Q646755}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama, Chiba]] neighborhood of Hachiman in [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|qq=|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. [[sn:commons:Category:Tsurugaya-Hachiman-gū]][[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11676182]] Wikidata name: Tsurugaya Hachimangū [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:10, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG | location = [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[:en:Tateyama|Tateyama]], [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35.005239|N|139.866667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Chūai|WD=Q179971}}; {{ill|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803}}; {{ill|Ōjin|WD=Q317997}} | founding = Early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[:en:Respect for the Aged Day|Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|WD=Q646755}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama, Chiba]] neighborhood of Hachiman in [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takenouchi no Sukune|Takenouchi no Sukune]]. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]]. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi]]. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鶴谷八幡宮|1=Tsurugaya Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11676182}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|1=Kokufu-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11420919}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of [[:en:Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Tateyama Station]] on the [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Uchibō Line|Uchibō Line]]. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[sn:commons:Category:Tsurugaya-Hachiman-gū]][[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11676182]] Wikidata name: Tsurugaya Hachimangū [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 10:10, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū | image = File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, haiden.JPG | location = [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Hachiman]], [[:en:Tateyama|Tateyama]], [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]] | coordinates = {{Coord|35.005239|N|139.866667|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | deity = {{ill|Chūai|WD=Q179971}}; {{ill|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803}}; {{ill|Ōjin|WD=Q317997}} | founding = Early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] | structure = | type = [[Awa Province|Awa]] [[:en:Sōja|Sōja]]
Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[:en:Respect for the Aged Day|Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|WD=Q646755}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama, Chiba]] neighborhood of Hachiman in [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takenouchi no Sukune|Takenouchi no Sukune]]. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]]. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi]]. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鶴谷八幡宮|1=Tsurugaya Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11676182}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|1=Kokufu-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11420919}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of [[:en:Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Tateyama Station]] on the [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Uchibō Line|Uchibō Line]]. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before [[:en:Respect for the Aged Day|Respect for the Aged Day]]) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|WD=Q646755}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the [[:en:Tateyama, Chiba|Tateyama, Chiba]] neighborhood of Hachiman in [[:en:Chiba Prefecture|Chiba Prefecture]]. Historically, it served as the [[:en:Sōja shrine|Sōja]] (provincial shrine) for [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]]. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]] under the influence of the [[:en:Minamoto clan|Minamoto clan]]. The shrine received patronage from the [[:en:Satomi clan|Satomi clan]] during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the [[:en:Kyōhō|Kyōhō era]]; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takenouchi no Sukune|Takenouchi no Sukune]]. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]]. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to [[:en:Kotoshironushi|Kotoshironushi]]. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鶴谷八幡宮|1=Tsurugaya Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11676182}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|1=Kokufu-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11420919}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of [[:en:Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Tateyama Station]] on the [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] [[:en:Uchibō Line|Uchibō Line]]. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|1=list of Shinto shrines in Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11506049}} * [[:en:Hachiman shrine|Hachiman shrine]] == External Links == * [http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:word=11010 Official website] (Japanese) {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|鶴谷八幡宮|version=101066790|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:鶴谷八幡宮]] [[Category:Hachiman faith]] [[Category:Hachiman shrines]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Chiba Prefecture]] [[Category:Awa Province (Chiba)]] [[Category:Top 500 Attractions of Bōsō Peninsula]] [[Category:Prefecturally designated intangible folk cultural property]] [[Category:Buildings in Tateyama, Chiba]] [[Category:History of Tateyama, Chiba]] {{Commons category|Tsurugaya-Hachiman-gū}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q11676182}}

Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * [[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Hachiman]] (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * [[:en:Emperor Chūai|Chūai]] (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * [[:en:Empress Jingū|Empress Jingū]] (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early [[:en:Heian period|Heian period]] near the provincial capital of [[:en:Awa Province (Chiba)|Awa Province (Chiba)]] in what is now [[:en:Minamibōsō|Minamibōsō]]. Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before {{ill|Respect for the Aged Day|en|Respect for the Aged Day|WD=Q1186127|lt=Respect for the Aged Day}}) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|WD=Q646755}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama, Chiba}} neighborhood of Hachiman in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|en|Awa Province (Chiba)|WD=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province (Chiba)}}. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Hachiman}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|WD=Q179971|lt=Chūai}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|en|Awa Province (Chiba)|WD=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province (Chiba)}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|en|Minamibōsō|WD=Q873521|lt=Minamibōsō}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|en|Minamoto clan|WD=Q599881|lt=Minamoto clan}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|en|Satomi clan|WD=Q2975367|lt=Satomi clan}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō era}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|en|Takenouchi no Sukune|WD=Q1073668|lt=Takenouchi no Sukune}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|Takemikazuchi|WD=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|en|Kotoshironushi|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鶴谷八幡宮|1=Tsurugaya Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11676182}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|1=Kokufu-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11420919}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Honden (Structure) ** Ceiling carvings of "One Hundred Dragons" (Sculpture) == Access == '''location''': 68 Hachiman, Tateyama, Chiba Prefecture, Japan '''Transportation''': 1 km north of {{ill|Tateyama Station (Chiba)|en|Tateyama Station (Chiba)|WD=Q553883|lt=Tateyama Station}} on the {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|WD=Q499071|lt=East Japan Railway Company}} {{ill|Uchibō Line|en|Uchibō Line|WD=Q1142964|lt=Uchibō Line}}. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shinto shrines|ja|日本の神社一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shinto shrines|1=list of Shinto shrines in Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11506049}} * {{ill|Hachiman shrine|en|Hachiman shrine|WD=Q11390939|lt=Hachiman shrine}} == External Links Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before {{ill|Respect for the Aged Day|en|Respect for the Aged Day|WD=Q1186127|lt=Respect for the Aged Day}}) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|WD=Q646755}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama, Chiba}} neighborhood of Hachiman in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|en|Awa Province (Chiba)|WD=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province (Chiba)}}. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Hachiman}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|WD=Q179971|lt=Chūai}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|en|Awa Province (Chiba)|WD=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province (Chiba)}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|en|Minamibōsō|WD=Q873521|lt=Minamibōsō}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}} under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|en|Minamoto clan|WD=Q599881|lt=Minamoto clan}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|en|Satomi clan|WD=Q2975367|lt=Satomi clan}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō era}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, honden.JPG|Honden (City Cultural Property) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, yohaijo.JPG|Awa Shrine Yohai-jo (viewing platform for distant worship) File:Tsurugaya-hachimangu, otorii.JPG|Otorii (Main Gate) == Subordinate Shrines == * '''Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}} (Ōzake no Mikoto). * '''Takara Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|en|Takenouchi no Sukune|WD=Q1073668|lt=Takenouchi no Sukune}}. * '''Kashima Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Takemikazuchi|en|Takemikazuchi|WD=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi}}. * '''Nishinomiya Shrine''': Dedicated to {{ill|Kotoshironushi|en|Kotoshironushi|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi}}. == festivals == The shrine's most notable event is its festival, known as {{ill|Yawatanmachi|ja|やわたんまち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yawatanmachi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鶴谷八幡宮|1=Tsurugaya Hachimangū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11676182}}, designated as a {{ill|Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja|千葉県指定文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chiba Prefectural Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|1=Kokufu-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11420919}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' ** Former [[Ken-sha]] | festivals = Mid-September (weekend before {{ill|Respect for the Aged Day|en|Respect for the Aged Day|WD=Q1186127|lt=Respect for the Aged Day|1=Respect for the Aged Day}}) | map = {{location map|Japan Chiba|lat_deg=35|lat_min=0|lat_sec=18.8|lon_deg=139|lon_min=52|lon_sec=0|label=Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū|position=right|width=210|float=center|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|caption=}} | prefecture= {{ill|Tateyama|WD=Q646755|1=Tateyama, Chiba}} }} '''Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū''' (鶴谷八幡宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|en|Tateyama, Chiba|WD=Q646755|lt=Tateyama, Chiba|1=Tateyama, Chiba}} neighborhood of Hachiman in {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|WD=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture|1=Chiba Prefecture}}. Historically, it served as the {{ill|Sōja shrine|en|Sōja shrine|WD=Q1107129|lt=Sōja|1=Sōja shrine}} (provincial shrine) for {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|en|Awa Province (Chiba)|WD=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province (Chiba)|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}}. Under the modern shrine Ranking system, it held the Rank of a {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|1=Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine enshrines three principal kami: * {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Hachiman|1=Emperor Ōjin}} (品陀和気命, Emperor Ōjin) * {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|WD=Q179971|lt=Chūai|1=Emperor Chūai}} (帯中津彦命, Emperor Chūai) * {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|WD=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū|1=Empress Jingū}} (息長帯姫命, Empress Jingū) == History == The shrine was established during the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|WD=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}} near the provincial capital of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|en|Awa Province (Chiba)|WD=Q1053044|lt=Awa Province (Chiba)|1=Awa Province (Chiba)}} in what is now {{ill|Minamibōsō|en|Minamibōsō|WD=Q873521|lt=Minamibōsō|1=Minamibōsō}}. Originally created as the sōja shrine of Awa Province, it was converted into a Hachiman shrine due to the growing popularity of Hachiman worship during the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}} under the influence of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|en|Minamoto clan|WD=Q599881|lt=Minamoto clan|1=Minamoto clan}}. The shrine received patronage from the {{ill|Satomi clan|en|Satomi clan|WD=Q2975367|lt=Satomi clan|1=Satomi clan}} during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|1=Sengoku Period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q117415390}} and later from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}. It was formally renamed "Tsurugaya Hachiman-gū" in 1976 after a major restoration project to celebrate its 1000th anniversary. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine complex includes several important structures: * '''Honden''': Constructed in 1721 during the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō era|1=Kyōhō}}; designated as a Tateyama City Cultural Property. * '''Heiden and Haiden''': Rebuilt in 1932 after the original buildings were destroyed in the [[:en:1923 Great Kantō earthquake|1923 Great Kantō earthquake]]. * '''Shamusho''': Administrative building. This festival preserves elements of the ancient {{ill|Kokufu-sai|ja|国府祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokufu-sai|1=Kokufu-sai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11420919}} and has been held for over 1000 years. == Cultural Properties == * '''Chiba Prefectural Cultural Properties''' ** Yawatanmachi festival (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) * '''Tateyama City Cultural Properties''' **
